analytics_minimization_note: Use shared public tokens and bounded aggregate metrics by default; avoid individualized voter-tracking or household-specific QR destinations in ordinary public-help materials.
auto_action_boundary_note: Do not use QR or shortlink handoffs as the primary path to force a download, app install, text message, or other surprise action; prefer a page with a clear call to action.
delivery_role_note: QR codes and short URLs bridge constrained public carriers into current official destinations, but the handoff layer does not become the rule source by itself.
handoff_surface_label: Example State official voter-information QR and shortlink surface
qr_text_fallback_policy_note: Every public QR intended to carry action-changing voter information keeps a nearby readable URL or office/help route so users who cannot or do not scan can still recover the same destination.
short_url_policy_note: Short URLs and vanity paths resolve to the most relevant current official destination, not to a generic homepage or opaque intermediate hop when a direct official landing page is available.
stale_recovery_policy_note: Old printed or posted handoff tokens are redirected to the current official destination when safe, or to a help-rich tombstone/replacement page when direct redirect would mislead.
trusted_domain_policy_note: Keep public QR and shortlink handoffs inside recognizable official government domains where possible, and prefer concise memorable paths over opaque third-party resolvers.
